strategy.summary: Reproduce the GH#9903 correctness bug in statsmodels.stats.diagnostic.linear_rainbow for use_distance=True by running the repository test(s) that assert order invariance and centroid-based equivalence. The buggy revision should fail because it orders by distance to an arbitrary middle-indexed observation (exog[nobs//2]) and uses unstable tie-breaking; additionally, constant-column exog could raise LinAlgError due to singular covariance (fixed version uses pseudo-inverse).

pinned_because: The defect is inside statsmodels.stats.diagnostic.linear_rainbow; to transition buggy->fixed you must test the repo code at two specific revisions (c14824302280 for buggy, the PR merge commit for fixed). The strategy below assumes you will build/test from the git working tree (not only from nightly wheels).

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision (commit c14824302280), the test suite marked above fails: the computed rainbow statistic for use_distance=True differs across permutations of rows (order dependence), and/or the constant-column case raises LinAlgError (singular covariance). On the fixed revision (the PR #9903 fix), all these tests pass: the statistic is invariant to permutation up to floating-point noise, and passing center with use_distance=True emits a FutureWarning and does not change the result.
strategy.numerical_probe: Permutation invariance of linear_rainbow(res, use_distance=True) for the same data with different row orders; optionally compare to manual centroid-based Mahalanobis ordering using np.linalg.pinv(np.cov(...)) and einsum for distances; also check deprecated center keyword behavior under use_distance=True.

input_output_examples.input: Call statsmodels.stats.diagnostic.linear_rainbow with use_distance=True and permuted rows.
input_output_examples.buggy_output: Test assertion fails because the statistic is not identical across permutations (order dependence).
input_output_examples.expected_output: Test assertion passes because the statistic is identical across permutations up to floating-point tolerance.

input_output_examples.input: Provide exog with a constant column (add_const=True) and use_distance=True.
input_output_examples.buggy_output: May raise LinAlgError on buggy revision due to singular covariance.
input_output_examples.expected_output: Fixed revision uses pseudo-inverse so no exception is raised and the statistic matches the reference across permutations.

input_output_examples.buggy_output: Either center changes the result or no FutureWarning is emitted.
input_output_examples.expected_output: Fixed revision emits FutureWarning matching "center keyword is deprecated" and returns the same statistic as the call without center.

risks: Toolchain variability: exact failure mode (assertion mismatch vs exception) may depend on numpy/scipy BLAS/LAPACK implementations; the test should still fail on buggy code because it is logically order dependent, but floating-point behavior could shift the mismatch magnitude.

Platform/arch dependence: if a given BLAS/LAPACK version happens to mask the singular-covariance issue (constant-column case), the permutation-invariance tests should still catch the bug; however, if it doesn’t, ensure you run all four tests listed in the -k expression.

Build/packaging: you must run tests against the repository code at the specified commits; installing from nightly wheels alone may not reproduce the buggy revision unless that wheel corresponds exactly to c14824302280.

Era constraints were unbounded (no documented constraint/ceiling for statsmodels or numpy/scipy stack); you must choose compatible versions. The transition property (buggy->fixed) should hold across a reasonable scientific-python stack, but if you hit unrelated numerical differences, ensure you’re using the repo’s CI-compatible dependency versions.

oracle.reference_source: Reference is computed inside the test as ref = smsdia.linear_rainbow(res, use_distance=True) from the unpermuted dataset; then each permuted-statistic must match via assert_allclose.
oracle.why: The project’s own test defines the oracle: invariant statistic equality between ref and permuted calls, plus a FutureWarning requirement for the deprecated center keyword. There is no external numeric gold value; the correctness condition is invariance/equivalence.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: test_rainbow_use_distance_order_invariant (and/or the discrete variant, and/or centroid equivalence) fails because linear_rainbow(use_distance=True) returns a different statistic after permuting rows. If add_const=True, the buggy implementation may also raise LinAlgError due to singular covariance (missing pseudo-inverse handling).
strategy.passes_on_fixed: test_rainbow_use_distance_order_invariant, test_rainbow_use_distance_order_invariant_discrete, test_rainbow_use_distance_matches_manual_ordering, and test_rainbow_center_deprecated all pass: use_distance=True orders by Mahalanobis distances to the exog centroid using a pseudo-inverse so results are permutation invariant and constant/rank-deficient designs do not error; center emits FutureWarning and does not affect results.
